parts:
Sorry for the delay in replying, your message got caught by the Google Groups spam filter.

We hope to make file monitoring much, much nicer in the future, but for now here's what you can do:

Let's say you have a function getLatestFile() that knows what directory to look in and how to identify the latest file. You could put this at the very top of your server.R (outside of shinyServer()):

values <- reactiveValues()
values$file <- getLatestFile()
observe({
  invalidateLater(10 * 60 * 1000)  # 10 minutes, in milliseconds
  values$file <- getLatestFile()
})

Then everywhere you need to refer to the filename, you will read from "values$file". The "observe" code block will execute every 10 minutes, and if values$file ever changes, then any reactive expressions/outputs that depend on its value will know they need to reexecute.

I don't know if there is an easy way to drop a dynamic header title into headerPanel, but if you can just have the date stamp shown somewhere else then it's easy, just use a textOutput along with renderText.



On Mon, Apr 29, 2013 at 6:00 PM, Wei Hu <andre...@gmail.com> wrote:
Shiny is AWESOME! Now I'm building a reporting facility to show "fancy" plots and statistics to my business users by Shiny. I would like to reload some data files after they are generated everyday and pass in the "date" into server.R. Say in the header, i would like to show "My Shiny App on ${date}". These are the possible solutions I can think of:
 
1) Set up a daily cronjob which restarts the server.R at a time all the new files have already been generated. But how to pass in the "date" as a parameter? Environment variable could be a solution, but is there a neater one?
 
2) Loop w/ sleep inside server.R to check file existences and get the "date" from the file names. Guess multithreading in R are needed in this case...
 
3) When the files got generated, send a URL with "date" as parameters.
 
Any better ideas?
 
Thanks,
Andrew
